base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and purchase an e-reader. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking to buy an e-reader. I've narrowed it down to 3 models.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 e-readers: the Kindle Scribe, the Kobo Libra Colour, and the Kindle Paperwhite

Kindle Scribe: 10.2-inch screen, stylus included, note-taking features, $340. Kobo Libra Colour: 7-inch colour e-ink, stylus-compatible, library integration, $220. Kindle Paperwhite: 6.8-inch standard e-ink, waterproof, long battery life, $150.
User mostly reads novels and occasionally borrows library ebooks, reads before bed

constraints.value: Maximum budget is $160 (computed from monthly income $2400, rule: never spend more than one day's pay on a gadget, $2400 / 15 working days = $160)
constraints.surface_form: I make about $2400 a month across 15 paid days. My personal rule is I never spend more than one day's pay on a gadget — keeps me from impulse buying expensive stuff.
inference_chain: $2400 monthly income ÷ 15 working days per month = $160 per working day
Personal rule: never spend more than one day's pay on a gadget

constraints.value: User does not need note-taking or stylus features, only reads novels
constraints.surface_form: I don't really take notes or annotate — I just want something for reading novels in bed
inference_chain: Only reads novels → no need for stylus or note-taking
No stylus need → Kindle Scribe's main feature is irrelevant
No stylus need → Kobo Libra Colour's stylus compatibility is irrelevant

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 e-readers (Kindle Scribe, Kobo Libra Colour, Kindle Paperwhite). You will share device details, your income and spending rule, and your reading habits across several turns. Your colleague and friend will praise the Kindle Scribe and Kobo Libra Colour. At the very end, you will say you have decided and need to finalize your purchase — you must NEVER name which e-reader you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person. You share information matter-of-factly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience. When mentioning friends or colleagues, you relay their experiences casually.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could cause identity confusion

aims.description: I'm looking to buy an e-reader. I've narrowed it down to 3 models — the Kindle Scribe, the Kobo Libra Colour, and the Kindle Paperwhite.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option decision framework

aims.description: So the Kindle Scribe is the big one — 10.2-inch screen, comes with a stylus, great for note-taking, it's $340. The Kobo Libra Colour has a 7-inch colour e-ink display, stylus-compatible, integrates with my library app, that's $220. And the Kindle Paperwhite is 6.8-inch standard e-ink, waterproof, amazing battery life, $150.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 options with their prices and attributes
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with prices and features in ONE turn

aims.description: My colleague at work got the Kindle Scribe a few months ago. She uses it for meeting notes and says the writing feel is incredible — almost like real paper. She takes it everywhere.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Kindle Scribe review

drift_config.drift_topic: bought Kindle Scribe, uses it for meeting notes, writing feel is incredible, takes it everywhere

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Kindle Scribe

aims.description: I make about $2400 a month across 15 paid days. My personal rule is I never spend more than one day's pay on a gadget — keeps me from impulse buying expensive stuff.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the spending rule and ideally computes $2400 / 15 working days = $160 cap
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via income + spending rule — requires computation to derive $160 cap

aims.description: My colleague was showing me how she annotates PDFs on the Scribe — she highlights passages and writes in the margins. The screen size makes a huge difference for that kind of thing apparently.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more Kindle Scribe praise

drift_config.drift_topic: annotates PDFs on Scribe, highlights and writes in margins, screen size is great for it

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Kindle Scribe (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I don't really take notes or annotate — I just want something for reading novels in bed. I also borrow ebooks from the library sometimes.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes that stylus/note-taking features are irrelevant for this user
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver use-case constraint — eliminates the premium features of Scribe and Kobo Colour as unnecessary

aims.description: My friend just got the Kobo Libra Colour last week. He's really into manga and says the colour e-ink makes a world of difference for comics. He was raving about how sharp the panels look.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Kobo Libra Colour review

drift_config.drift_topic: got Kobo Libra Colour, loves it for manga, colour e-ink makes comics look sharp

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Kobo Libra Colour

aims.description: He also mentioned the Kobo store has way more international titles and the library integration is seamless — he borrows graphic novels through it all the time.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more Kobo Libra Colour praise

drift_config.drift_topic: Kobo store has more international titles, library integration is seamless for graphic novels

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Kobo Libra Colour (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: Alright I've made up my mind. I need to finalize my purchase this week — which one should I go with?
aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends the Kindle Paperwhite ($150), the only option within the computed $160 budget cap that matches the user's novel-reading use case
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to the constraint-compliant option (Kindle Paperwhite)

ground_truth.answer: The user should buy the Kindle Paperwhite ($150). The Kindle Scribe ($340) and Kobo Libra Colour ($220) both exceed the $160 budget cap derived from $2400 monthly income ÷ 15 working days = $160 per day. Additionally, the user only reads novels and doesn't need stylus or note-taking features, making the premium features of the Scribe and Kobo Colour unnecessary. Only the Kindle Paperwhite ($150 < $160, pure reading device, waterproof for bedtime reading) satisfies all constraints.
required_elements: Agent recommends the Kindle Paperwhite specifically
Agent shows that the budget cap is $160 by computing $2400 monthly income ÷ 15 working days = $160 per working day
Agent shows that the Kindle Scribe at $340 exceeds the derived $160 budget cap
Agent shows that the Kobo Libra Colour at $220 exceeds the derived $160 budget cap
Agent identifies that the Kindle Paperwhite at $150 fits within the $160 budget
forbidden_elements: Recommending the Kindle Scribe ($340 is more than double the $160 budget cap)
Recommending the Kobo Libra Colour ($220 exceeds the $160 budget cap by 37%)
Ignoring the spending rule when making a recommendation
Asking the user which e-reader they decided on instead of computing the answer from constraints
Saying the decision depends on the user's preference without committing to an option
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $2400 monthly income ÷ 15 working days = $160 max gadget spend. Kindle Scribe $340 > $160 (eliminated). Kobo Libra Colour $220 > $160 (eliminated). Kindle Paperwhite $150 < $160 (passes). Use-case constraint: user only reads novels, no note-taking needed — Scribe's stylus and Kobo's colour display are unnecessary premium features. Despite 4 drift turns praising the Scribe (colleague's meeting notes) and Kobo Colour (friend's manga), the agent must respect the hard budget constraint and recommend the Paperwhite.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
